As a Lead Manager, you will be the main point of contact for warm leads: following up with prospects, building rapport, and guiding them until they are ready to close or speak with our acquisitions closer. Additionally, you will engage in targeted outbound prospecting, using our high-quality data (e.g. fresh county records for probate and foreclosures) to initiate conversations with potential sellers. This hybrid role is critical – you'll keep our funnel organized and full by both managing incoming leads and proactively hunting new ones. If you are a people-person who is also organized and driven, this could be a perfect fit. Who We Are: The OmniKey Group is founded and led by top-ranking Fortune 500 Sales Managers with a proven track record of developing and employing elite talent. We don't just build businesses — we build careers. As we scale aggressively, we are looking for driven individuals who want to grow alongside a leadership team that knows how to invest in people. Responsibilities: Lead Nurturing: Manage a pipeline of ~50 active leads in our CRM. Promptly follow up with interested home sellers via phone, text, and email . Your goal is to build relationships over time – check in regularly, understand their situation, and keep our company top-of-mind for when they're ready to sell. Initial Lead Qualification: Call new inquiries (from inbound calls or web forms) as soon as they come in. Have a friendly introductory conversation to gather information: Why might they sell? When? What's the property condition? Identify serious motivation versus casual interest. Ensure every new lead is contacted and categorized (hot, warm, long-term, etc.). Set Appointments: When a lead is qualified and shows strong interest/motivation, schedule an appointment or transfer the call to our acquisitions closer. You control the calendar for our acquisition team – scheduling consultations or property visits. Make sure our closer gets all key information before the meeting. Outbound Prospecting: Devote part of your time to reaching out to cold prospects from our premium data lists (such as probate, pre-foreclosure, or other niche lists we've pulled). Use cold calling or personalized texts/emails to introduce our service and see if they have a property they might consider selling. This "deep prospecting" uses the valuable data provided by our Data Manager to generate new leads beyond the ones who come to us. Pipeline Organization: Keep the CRM updated meticulously. Log every call, update lead statuses, and add detailed notes after each contact. Set follow-up reminders for each lead so you always remember to call back when promised. No lead should ever be forgotten or left without a next action. Team Coordination: Work closely with the acquisitions (closing) team. Clearly hand off highly motivated leads with full context (notes about the seller's situation, motivation level, etc.). After our closer makes an offer, circle back with the seller to address any concerns or continue nurturing if they didn't sign immediately. Essentially, you bridge the gap between initial interest and closed deal, keeping communication smooth. Requirements: Excellent Communication: Fluent English speaker who can converse naturally and confidently with U.S. homeowners. You have a friendly phone demeanor, active listening skills, and can build trust over multiple conversations. (Experience talking to older American homeowners is a plus – you can strike the right tone of patience and professionalism.) Sales/Customer Service Experience: 1+ year in a role like sales representative, account manager, customer service, or any position requiring consistent client follow-up. Real estate experience (especially in investing or related to motivated sellers) is highly advantageous – if you've dealt with sellers or real estate leads before, let us know! Follow-Up and Organizational Skills: A proven ability to juggle dozens of leads and keep an organized system. You never let a task or callback slip. Using a CRM or lead management system should be second nature to you. (If you pride yourself on color-coded spreadsheets or meticulous task lists, that's a good sign!)Google Drive Persuasion & Empathy: You know how to connect with people, ask the right questions, and handle objections. You're empathetic to sellers' situations (many may be in tough circumstances like foreclosure, probate, etc.) and also persuasive in highlighting how our service can help them. Tech-Savvy: Comfortable with CRM software, click-to-call phone systems, and general productivity tools (Google Workspace, etc.). Able to learn new apps quickly. Also, must have reliable internet and a headset/quiet workspace for frequent calls. Work Hours: Available to work full-time on US hours (e.g. 9am–6pm PST). Leads must be called quickly during da ---------- hours in the US. Flexibility to occasionally adjust hours for an urgent lead is appreciated. We are seeking someone who can commit long-term (12+ months) and become an integral part of the team. What We Offer: Base Pay + Commission: Competitive base salary plus commission on each deal you help close. Your earning potential grows with every deal. Impactful Work: This role is at the heart of our business – you will directly influence our revenue by turning leads into deals. It's rewarding to see your relationship-building result in a family helped and a successful transaction. We often deal with homeowners in difficult situations; you'll take pride in guiding them toward a solution. Training & Development: We will provide training on our scripts, CRM, and the real estate investment process. Team Environment: Work with a supportive, growth-minded team. We maintain open communication and regular team check-ins despite being remote. You'll get feedback and recognition for your hard work. We also encourage new ideas – if you have suggestions to improve our follow-up processes, we want to hear them. Remote Work Lifestyle: This is a 100% remote position. Save on commute time and work from the comfort of your home (or home office). As long as you can reliably cover the required hours and stay connected, you'll enjoy the flexibility of remote work. Qualified candidates will be invited to a Zoom interview (and possibly a role-play exercise). Come join a team where your follow-up prowess will be highly valued and rewarded!

title: Operations & Project Execution (Fast Growing)
description: Operations Manager-Execution Partner-Project Killer-Fast-Growing Comic Book Company Own the operations backbone of a niche comic book brand, work directly with leadership, and get promoted fairly by numbers. This role is for that special person who wants to become truly exceptional. If that’s you, you already know this message is your signal. Lots of freedom to figure it out, great for someone that loves building with Legos - Direct proximity to leadership: you work daily with the Ops Manager on the most important projects in the company. - Clear advancement path: your growth is tied to visible numbers (tasks shipped, zero-miss cadence, freed founder/ops time, profit/leading metrics), not politics. - Insane skill growth: the pace and standards here mean every 12 months with us will feel like 3 years of experience in a normal VA/ops role. You can leapfrog your friends. If you join this will change your life. You will work harder than you’ve ever worked before and grow faster than you’ve ever grown before. - Comic Books!: you’re not just pushing random SaaS tickets; you’re inside a real comic book store seeing rare old comic books, private deals, and the business behind the Hollywood Marvel Movies that everyone loves! If you’re that person who enjoys working really hard to the point that it takes 2-3 people to do what you did listen up: Our tasks in asana for projects and ongoing operations are moving at a snail’s pace. Ops Manager + CEO is chasing tasks, slack policing, cleaning up Asana, and re-explaining context instead of focusing on their jobs. We’ve had “pleasant” VAs who: Can’t drive tasks to completion independently Mark tasks complete with no proof Miss reports/skip cadence and require chasing. Drift on ownership, urgency & follow thru Need hand-holding I don’t need another task hopper. I need a project killer who comes into ambiguity, creates structure, drives tasks to completion, and actually frees the Ops Manager to focus on his key projects. If this works, his deep work hours and project output go up because you’re handling everything else. We will measure that and tie your promotions/raises to it. This is not for everyone. We’re looking for winners. What You’ll Actually Do You will be Ops Manager’s execution partner and force-multiplier. Concrete outputs: Own Asana: every task has an owner, due date, Done Check, and proof link when completed Maintain an active queue of 20+ meaningful tasks, prioritized against our key rocks (Marketing, Sales, Ongoing Operations, Cleanup, Admin) Ship 25+ tasks/week with proof, minimal rework, and zero “ghosted” items Proactively handle operational issues/fires in designated lanes Maintain Reporting at Set Cadence, Follow-up loops across projects Add leverage: plug AI into our workflows (Asana, docs, reports) to make us faster and cleaner without being asked We do NOT need more SOPS-although you might tighten them on the fly. We need someone to do the operations. If you want to sit and write playbooks all day, this is the wrong seat-that will be an earned responsibility later. If you aren’t ready to work hard daily do not apply. How We Set You Up To Win (First 90 Days) We don’t just throw you in the deep end. In your first 30 days, you’ll shadow the Ops Manager, learn our Asana + reporting systems, and get a clear scorecard so you always know what “great” looks like. By 30 days, you’ll own your own project lanes with weekly 1:1s for feedback, support, and removing blockers so you can move faster instead of guessing what we want. Real Growth Example One of our Filipino teammates started with us on basic execution work at ~$800/month. Over time, he took ownership of his queue, fixed broken processes, and became the person we trusted to “just handle it.” As his scope grew, so did his comp and stability. Now he makes ~$2,500/month (and we’re working on getting him even more) because he stuck with it and actually grew. A lot of people say they want that, but their resumes show 6–12 month hops. The pattern here is simple: prove you can own outcomes over time, and we grow your responsibilities, trust, and pay accordingly. Schedule, Hours & Time Zone (No Surprises) This is a full time, US hours role (roughly US Eastern business hours) with a true 50–60 hour workweek during this growth season. Expect most weeks to be closer to that 60 hour mark. If you want a strict 40 hour cap, this is the wrong seat; if you want a place where extra effort is noticed, measured, and rewarded, you’ll feel at home here. This is not just a job. This is a commitment. What Winning Looks Like By Day 30: Ops Manager is spending ~95% of his time on projects, not Slack/Asana/admin fires, because you’re handling those and executing projects alongside him. Profit and leading metrics are moving up faster because of you By 12 months: You are Ops Manager’s go to operator & on track to become Ops Manager. Nothing important moves in Ops without you knowing. You own the Asana board, key ops projects, and reporting cadence. You’re the person we trust to “just handle it,” and your comp reflects that increased ownership. If you become that go to operator, you’ll have real say in how we run Ops – you won’t just be ‘executing tickets,’ you’ll help design the system.” Who This Is NOT For You prefer to ‘coordinate’ and assign tasks to others instead of doing the work yourself with excellence. You want to manage people before you’ve truly proven you can personally execute at a high level. You want a chill, low-pressure 9–5 You need to be told what to do all day and hate being judged by objective numbers You mark tasks complete without proof or next steps You change jobs every 6–18 months and blame the company/manager/market/ You get defensive or freeze when given direct feedback or pressure You are currently juggling multiple full time clients and want to “squeeze us in” on the side. You are mass applying to dozens of jobs and just want to see who bites first. Who This IS For You’ve stayed 2–3+ years in at least one role and can prove outcomes You like pressure, highly competitive environments, being the one who “gets it done” when others stall You’ve built systems (trackers, automations, SOPs), not just followed them You are tech-comfortable: Asana (or similar), CRMs, zaps, AI tools, simple web/ops/marketing stacks You’re willing to bet on one company instead of juggling lots of smaller, easier gigs. You hate corporate BS– endless meetings, vague goals, and politics – and would rather be rewarded for what you actually create. You’re happy to grind 50–60 hours/week no issues. We’re in a BIG growth & push season. It will be like this for the next year and then we’ll see. Everyone wants to grow a lot, but it’s actually happening here. Comp & Growth (All of this is written into your contract.) Months 1–3: Ramp / Trial • $800/month base, guaranteed, while you learn our systems and we test fit. • No bonus in this phase. You’re paid to prove you can hit the KPI floors. Month 4+ – Performance Based Upside • Base stays at $800 until you’ve hit KPI floors for 2 straight months. After that, base increases to $900/month going forward. • On top of base, you can earn: $400 bonus in months where you hit 3 out of 4 KPIs (with Output as one of them). $1,000 bonus in months where you hit 4 out of 4 KPIs on the weekly scorecard. • In practice, that means: Solid performance months ~$1,200–$1,300/month Killer months (4/4 KPIs)~$1,800–$1,900/month All bonuses are 100% KPI based  (shipped outcomes, taking load off the Ops Manager, zero CEO/manager rescues, tight open loops) and 4/5 culture. Training & Growth Investment (on top of pay) We actively invest in making you a sharper teammate. Over time, we’ll put thousands of dollars into your development (courses, coaching, playbooks, and tools) that we choose together based on what will make you more effective in this seat. We also protect uninterrupted deep work blocks for you every week (no rando ---------- etings, no Slack spam). You’re paid to ship outcomes, not sit in back to back Zoom calls. Important: This is an ON FIELD role. You will not have a team under you to delegate to. 95% of your time is doing the work yourself, 5% is light coordination. If your default mode is to make plans and pass tasks to others, this will be a bad fit. Compensation here is performance based. Raises are earned through clearly exceeding KPIs and demonstrating core values consistently. If you want “stability” to mean “I can coast and still get raises,” this won’t feel stable. If you want stability to mean “the better I get, the more valuable and secure I become,” you’ll like it here. How To Apply (24-Hour Test) Our Hiring Process (So There Are No Surprises) If your 24 hour answers impress us, the next steps are: A short interview focused on your past execution. A live 60 minute work trial inside our real tools where you’ll work directly with the Ops Manager. We do this because talk is cheap. If you don’t like being tested on real work before getting hired, this won’t be a fit. Do NOT click quick-apply. In the next 24 hours, you must: Reply with answers to ALL of these (short but specific; bullets are fine): Q1: Describe the most complex project you personally drove fro ---------- ssy start to completion where you did most of the execution yourself, not just assigning tasks. Include at least one example of how you set your own deadlines and moved forward when other people were slow to respond.” Q2: Share 3 links or screenshots (Google Docs, Sheets, Asana boards, trackers, automations, etc.) that you built yourself which show how you organize and drive work. Briefly explain each. Q3: You have 30 tasks due this week and realize you’ll miss 5. Walk me through, step-by-step, how you handle it with your manager and stakeholders. Q4:  Below are 6 messy “tasks” we actually see (all dumped into one list): – “Fix Asana, it’s a mess” – “Seller lead texting follow up??” – “Finance com/projections cadence d2 ” – “Inventory backlog insane” – “Need better reporting” – “Update SOPs In this role you will NOT have anyone to delegate to assume it’s just you and the Ops Manager. In a Google Doc, please: Rewrite these into clear tasks with: Owner (you or Ops Manager), Due Date (next 7–30 days), and a concrete Done Check + proof required. “Write your task descriptions as if you are committing: ‘I will do X by Y time. If Z doesn’t happen by [time], here’s my fallback.’ Generic ‘follow up / request access’ answers will fail you.” Put them in the order you’d actually do them and explain why in 3–5 bullet points. Link the Google Doc here (view access). Spend no more than 30–45 minutes. If you can’t figure this out on your own, this role will be too hard in real life – that’s okay, just skip applying. title: PriceLabs Revenue & Pricing Strategist
description: We are seeking an experienced PriceLabs Revenue & Pricing Strategist to lead our dynamic pricing and revenue management efforts across a portfolio of short-term rental properties. This role is responsible for optimizing pricing performance through data-driven analysis, strategic discounting, and targeted promotional initiatives. The ideal candidate will leverage PriceLabs to maximize Revenue per Available Rental (RevPAR), increase occupancy, and maintain competitive, market-responsive pricing strategies while balancing strong Average Daily Rates (ADR) with booking volume. Key Responsibilities Occupancy-Based Pricing Management Utilize PriceLabs’ Occupancy-Based Adjustments (OBA) to dynamically optimize rates based on individual listing and portfolio-wide booking pace. Monitor occupancy trends and adjust pricing strategies to meet revenue and occupancy targets. Fine-tune pricing rules, booking windows, and demand-based adjustments to improve overall portfolio performance. Promotions & Discount Strategy Identify orphan gaps, low-demand periods, and shoulder seasons across property calendars. Develop and implement targeted pricing promotions, including: Last-minute discounts Orphan-day pricing strategies Length-of-stay incentives Seasonal and occupancy-driven promotions Continuously evaluate promotional effectiveness and adjust strategies as needed. Listing Performance Audits Conduct weekly and monthly performance reviews across the portfolio. Analyze booking trends, ADR, RevPAR, occupancy rates, and conversion metrics. Identify underperforming listings and implement corrective actions through: Base price adjustments Minimum stay modifications Premium and discount optimization Seasonal pricing refinements Market & Competitive Analysis Leverage PriceLabs Neighborhood Data and Market Dashboards to track: Competitor pricing Market demand trends Booking lead times Seasonal fluctuations Local events and demand drivers Recommend pricing adjustments based on market intelligence and evolving conditions. Revenue Strategy Execution Collaborate with Marketing and Operations teams to support occupancy and revenue objectives. Launch targeted promotional campaigns when occupancy falls below established thresholds. Provide insights and recommendations that align pricing strategies with broader business goals. Required Qualifications PriceLabs Expertise Minimum 1–2 years of hands-on experience managing pricing strategies within PriceLabs. Strong understanding of: Occupancy-Based Adjustments (OBA) Custom Pricing Profiles Minimum Stay Rules Price Floors and Ceilings Seasonal Pricing Settings Dynamic Pricing Customizations Revenue Management & Analytics Demonstrated understanding of key short-term rental performance metrics, including: Average Daily Rate (ADR) Revenue per Available Rental (RevPAR) Occupancy Rate Booking Pace Lead Time Analysis Ability to interpret data and translate insights into actionable pricing strategies. Channel & PMS Experience Experience managing dynamic pricing integrations across major booking platforms, including: Airbnb Vrbo ---------- Familiarity with Property Management Systems (PMS) and channel management tools. Strategic Problem Solving Strong analytical and decision-making skills. Ability to evaluate local market conditions and determine optimal pricing actions, including premium increases, discount strategies, and demand-based adjustments. Proactive approach to identifying revenue opportunities and mitigating occupancy risks. Preferred Qualifications Experience managing multi-property or portfolio-level pricing strategies. Knowledge of short-term rental revenue management best practices. Advanced spreadsheet and reporting skills (Excel or Google Sheets). Experience working remotely with cross-functional teams. Success Metrics Increased portfolio RevPAR and occupancy rates. Improved booking pace and calendar utilization. Effective reduction of orphan gaps and unbooked inventory. Achievement of revenue targets while maintaining competitive market positioning. Consistent optimization of ADR without sacrificing occupancy performance.
